posts.text: Economics Job Market Rumors started back when I was on the job market 20 years ago. I remember how much the uncertainty of getting a job makes you seek out any kind of info. But quality matters. An anon forum was never going to cut it. And it would breed bad behavior. It did.

posts.text: Implications for the Fed: good news. Disinflation, even as the Fed's been on hold so far this year, supports its stance. It's too soon to say whether a hold will be appropriate in September—more data coming—but the chances of a hike edged down some today.

Gotta give it Claude as a vacation planner. Less than two weeks ago I figured out some time off was a necessity. Gave me several options and it worked out so well. It even made fun of the books I tried to pack, calling them my job wearing a snorkel.
Vacay fun: tried to pick out a movie to watch together. 16 yo son said Obsession, I said Anaconda, and hubby was appalled at all the hotel options. Went out for ice cream at Chaps instead.
Today’s reflection: an intellectual commitment to principles doesn’t mean you live them fully. Also, octagon rooms are lovely. #Monticello

Implications for the Fed: good news. Disinflation, even as the Fed's been on hold so far this year, supports its stance. It's too soon to say whether a hold will be appropriate in September—more data coming—but the chances of a hike edged down some today.

The breadth of inflation narrowed in July, reducing one of the risks the Fed is monitoring. The share of the CPI basket with prices rising 5%+ fell in July and is back to the average levels in 1997-2005, when inflation was close to 2%. This may be the best news in today's report!
